ak.data_sources.kw: where does the data come from|data source|sources|where is the data from|which satellite|who provides|data from|origin of data
ak.data_sources.q: Where does the data come from?
ak.data_sources.a: Most data is from NASA: POWER for rain and temperature, MODIS for how green the land is, GIBS satellite maps, and OPERA/HLS for tank water. The forecast and live rain are from Open-Meteo, tank names from OpenStreetMap and land height from AWS terrain tiles. Those are not NASA data and are labelled that way.
ak.nasa_or_not.kw: is this nasa data|is it nasa|nasa or not|not nasa|which data is nasa|nasa data|open-meteo|openmeteo
ak.nasa_or_not.a: NASA: POWER (rain and temperature), MODIS (greenness), GIBS (satellite maps) and OPERA/HLS (tank water). Not NASA: the forecast, live rain and seasonal outlook (Open-Meteo), tank locations (OpenStreetMap), land height (AWS terrain tiles) and soil maps (SoilGrids). Every value on the site carries its source label.
ak.offline.kw: offline|no internet|without internet|install|install app|add to home screen|does it work offline|save for later
ak.offline.a: Yes, partly. You can add the site to your phone's home screen like an app, and pages you opened before still open without internet. Live rain, the forecast and the farm planner need internet.
ak.privacy.kw: privacy|private|my data|personal data|is my data safe|do you save|who sees|location saved|phone number|tracking|safe
ak.privacy.a: Most of the site needs no sign-in and saves nothing about you. Game progress stays only in your own browser. The trip planner uses your position only to ask for the weather there and does not save it. The farm planner stores your phone number and farm details on the server, only so your farms are private to you, and you can export or delete them.
ak.languages.a: Yes. Use the Sinhala and English buttons at the top right. Tamil is not available yet. The Sinhala text is a draft that a native speaker still needs to review, so tell us if a word is wrong.
ak.not_ai.kw: are you ai|are you a robot|are you chatgpt|is this ai|artificial intelligence|how do you work|how does the bot work|who are you|what are you|bot
ak.not_ai.a: No. I am a rule-based helper. I match your words to questions we have written answers for, and I answer tank questions straight from the data files, with the source. I do not guess or make things up. If I am not sure, I will say so and offer the closest questions.
ak.signal_meaning.kw: what does green mean|what does amber mean|what does red mean|signal meaning|traffic light|colour meaning|color meaning|green amber red|what is the signal|signal colours
ak.signal_meaning.q: What do green, amber and red mean?
ak.signal_meaning.a: The signal compares tank water now with the usual. Green: enough water for the usual plan, including full paddy. Amber: take care; short-duration paddy and bethma (sharing water) are safer. Red: water is short; choose crops that need little water. Where the tank water has not been checked yet, the site says so instead of guessing.
ak.bethma.kw: what is bethma|bethma|sharing water|share water|water sharing|bethma meaning|bethmaa|bedma
ak.bethma.a: Bethma is the old way of sharing in dry times: when the tank cannot water every field, farmers share the water and the land so everyone grows something instead of a few growing everything. The site suggests it when the signal is amber.
ak.maha_yala.kw: what is maha|what is yala|maha and yala|maha season|yala season|seasons|which season|when is maha|when is yala
ak.maha_yala.a: Maha is the main rainy season (roughly October to March) and Yala is the drier season (roughly April to September) in Sri Lanka's Dry Zone. Which crops suit a tank depends on the season and on how much water is left.
ak.onset.kw: rains started|onset|when did the rains start|late rains|rain start|start of the rains|rains late|rains delayed
ak.onset.a: It compares the day this season's rains really began with the usual day, using NASA POWER rain data. Late rains mean a later sowing time, so the sowing calendar moves with it.
ak.bad_water_data.kw: water not checked|not checked yet|cannot say yet|why no water|no water data|water data missing|why is there no tank water|why cannot say|unknown paddy
ak.bad_water_data.q: Why does it say 'water not checked yet'?
ak.bad_water_data.a: Satellite water measurements (NASA OPERA/HLS) have been processed for only a few tanks so far, because it is slow work. For the other tanks the site says 'not checked yet' and 'cannot say yet' for paddy rather than guess. Rain, heat and the rain-fed crop advice still work for every tank.
ak.forecast_trust.kw: can i trust the forecast|forecast accurate|forecast reliable|how accurate|how far ahead|16 day|forecast wrong|forecast reliability|forcast
ak.forecast_trust.a: The 16-day forecast is from weather models through Open-Meteo (not NASA data, not radar). It is good for the next few days and less certain after the first week, so check again nearer the day.
ak.live_rain.kw: live rain|rain now|raining now|heavy rain warning|rain alert|rain last hour|nowcast|rain in the last 24 hours|rain card
ak.live_rain.q: How does the live rain card work?
ak.live_rain.a: The card shows hourly rain for the last 24 hours and the next 12 hours from Open-Meteo (not NASA, not radar) and refreshes every 5 minutes while the page is open. A heavy-rain banner appears when an hour has about 7.6 mm or six hours have about 30 mm. Those limits are drafts.
ak.weekly_advice.kw: weekly advice|this week|advice this week|weekly message|whatsapp|share advice|week advice
ak.weekly_advice.a: Each tank has a 'This week's advice' page built from the saved data and a live forecast. You can send it by WhatsApp or copy the text. The limits behind it are drafts for an Agricultural Instructor to review.
ak.share_card.kw: share card|summary card|print summary|share my tank|download card|card
ak.share_card.q: How do I share my tank's summary?
ak.share_card.a: Open your tank and choose the Card page: it is a one-page summary you can print or share with your farmer organisation.
ak.advanced_view.kw: advanced view|simple view|show numbers|more details|numbers|simple mode|advanced mode
ak.advanced_view.q: How do I see the numbers?
ak.advanced_view.a: The site uses plain words first. Switch from Simple to Advanced at the top to see the numbers behind them, each with its source.
ak.el_nino.kw: el nino|elnino|el niño|la nina|warm sea|ocean warming|enso
ak.el_nino.a: El Niño is a warm patch of the Pacific that can change rain in some years. We tested whether it helps predict Sri Lankan rain here, and it did not beat simply using the usual rain, so the site shows it only as a count and does not use it for advice. The Little Lessons explain it for children.
ak.farm_planner.kw: farm planner|my farm plan|register my farm|crop plan|rotation|plan my farm|farm plan|sign in farm|add my farm|which crops for my farm
ak.farm_planner.q: How do I plan my own farm?
ak.farm_planner.a: Open 'My farm plan' in the menu, sign in with your phone number and a short code, and add your farm on the map. You get your land zones, the threats we can see, and three crop plans (usual, soil-building, water-saving), each with how sure we are and the rules used. These are suggestions to talk over with your Agricultural Instructor, not promises.
ak.lessons.kw: lessons|little lessons|stories|picture stories|what can i learn|topics|learn about|teach me|water cycle|global warming|wildfire|landslide|glacier
ak.lessons.a: Little Lessons has 16 picture stories: a raindrop's journey, Maha and Yala, a chain of tanks, eyes in the sky, bethma, big drinkers and small sippers, reading the weather, seed to harvest, fire in the dry forest, when a hill slides, El Niño, La Niña, carbon, the big water cycle, melting glaciers and global warming. Each ends with a small game that earns stars.
ak.games.kw: games|play|fun|game list|what games|little farmers|rain cloud|tank farmer|can i play
ak.games.a: Little Farmers' Games (match the crops, sort, grow, seasons), Rain Cloud (steer a cloud with a slider), Tank Farmer (feed thirsty crops), My Farm (plant and upgrade crops) and the Challenges for students. All of them earn drops, which count towards levels and badges.
ak.rewards_how.kw: how do i get drops|rewards|points|earn drops|how to earn|badges|how do rewards work|stars|drops
ak.rewards_how.a: You get 5 drops for each star, plus 5 for your first pass of a game, 5 for your first perfect score, 2 for your first reward each day and 10 for every new badge. Playing a game again only pays for stars above your best.
ak.levels.kw: levels|level up|my level|how many badges|badge list|next level
ak.levels.q: How do levels and badges work?
ak.levels.a: Your drops add up to a level. There are 19 badges for things like finishing lessons, perfect scores and growing crops. Open My rewards to see your level, your badges and which lessons you have done.
ak.certificate.a: Yes. The My rewards page has a certificate you can print with your name and level.
ak.my_farm_game.kw: my farm|plant crops|upgrade crops|cups|farm game|clash|grow crops game|tank farmer cups
ak.my_farm_game.a: Catch cups of water in Tank Farmer, then spend them in My Farm to plant 8 crops and upgrade each one up to level 5. An upgrade costs as many cups as the crop's real water need, so thirsty crops cost more.
ak.kids_games.kw: small children|little kids|for kids|young children|read aloud|kids games|toddler|match the crops|memory game
ak.kids_games.q: Which games are for small children?
ak.kids_games.a: Little Farmers' Games are tiny one-idea games for small children: match the crops (10 levels), sort, grow and seasons. A drop guide gives one short sentence and the sentence can be read aloud.
ak.challenges.a: Challenges are practice games for students: a quiz of fixed facts, a ladder and a weekly challenge that use real tank data.
ak.real_or_game.kw: is this real|real data|real or made up|are the pictures real|ai pictures|are lessons true|are games real|is the data real in games
ak.real_or_game.q: Is it real data or just a game?
ak.real_or_game.a: The lessons give general facts. Most games use game art, and the sea-warmth map in Rain Cloud is game art, not data. In Tank Farmer, how thirsty each crop is comes from real data. The pictures were made for learning, not real photos; the Image credits page says where each one comes from.
ak.parents.kw: parents|teacher|safe for children|is it safe|ads|accounts|login for kids|child safety
ak.parents.a: The learning end needs no account and has no leaderboard. Progress is saved only in this browser, and nothing about the child is sent anywhere. You can reset the progress on the My rewards page.
ak.officer_count.kw: how many tanks|how many red|how many amber|how many green|count of tanks|number of tanks|how many wewa|tanks are red|total tanks|red tanks count
ak.officer_count.q: How many tanks are in each signal?
ak.officer_count.a: Of {n} tanks: {red} red, {amber} amber, {green} green and {none} with no signal yet. {demo} of them are demo tanks and are included in these counts.
ak.officer_list_red.kw: which tanks are red|list red tanks|red tanks|tanks in trouble|worst tanks|which tanks need attention|tanks at risk|show red
ak.officer_list_red.a: Red tanks: {names}. Open the dashboard and tap the Red tile to see them all.
ak.dashboard_use.kw: how to use the dashboard|dashboard|what is on this page|officer dashboard|how do i read the table|columns|what do the columns mean|table
ak.dashboard_use.q: How do I read the dashboard?
ak.dashboard_use.a: Each row is one tank: signal, water versus usual, rain this season versus usual, when the rains started, forecast rain for the next 7 days, live rain for the next 6 hours and how green the land is. A dash means the value is not available; nothing is guessed. Tap a tank for its full advice.
ak.filters.kw: filter|search tank|sort|hide demo|find a tank|narrow down|filter by signal
ak.filters.q: How do I filter or search?
ak.filters.a: Tap a coloured tile to show only that signal, type in the search box to find a tank by name, choose how to sort, and tick 'hide demo tanks' to leave out the demo ones.
ak.csv_download.a: Yes. Use the CSV button to download the rows now on screen (after your filters). It opens in Excel or any spreadsheet program.
ak.print_report.a: Yes. The Print button gives a clean page of the rows on screen, with the controls left out.
ak.officer_signin.kw: sign in|login|log in|who can see this|register as officer|why do i need to sign in|officer account|password|access
ak.officer_signin.q: Why do I have to sign in?
ak.officer_signin.a: The officer dashboard is for registered officers. You sign in with your phone number and a short code, and your office must have registered that number. If you are refused, ask your office to add it. Note that the tank data files themselves are public; sign-in protects the dashboard screen.
ak.red_means.kw: what does red mean|red signal|why is it red|what to do when red|advice for red|red tank advice
ak.red_means.q: What does a red tank mean?
ak.red_means.a: Red means tank water is short compared with the usual. The advice is to choose crops that need little water instead of paddy. Where the water was not checked, the tank shows no signal rather than a guess.
ak.live6.kw: next 6 hours|live rain column|rain next six hours|live column|why is live empty|live values
ak.live6.a: It is a live forecast of rain expected in the next 6 hours, fetched when the page opens, from Open-Meteo (not NASA data). If it cannot be fetched, the cell shows a dash.
ak.greenness.a: Greenness is the NASA MODIS vegetation index (NDVI) around the tank: how green the land looks from space compared with usual. It is a hint about crops and rain, not a measurement of yield.
ak.demo_tanks.a: Three tanks are demo placeholders, marked 'Demo data'. They show how the site looks and are not real. Tick 'hide demo tanks' to leave them out.
ak.data_age.kw: how old is the data|when was it updated|last updated|data age|refresh|how often updated|is it up to date|update time
ak.data_age.a: Saved tank data (rain, water, advice) is updated when the data refresh runs, and each tank shows when it was last updated. The live columns and the heavy-rain warning are fetched when you open the page. NASA POWER rain currently ends on 30 September 2026.
ak.thresholds_draft.kw: thresholds|draft|limits|are the limits official|who set the limits|review|instructor review|are these official|cutoffs
ak.thresholds_draft.a: No. The limits behind the advice and warnings (in pipeline/config.toml and the crop facts) are drafts, each with its source and confidence, waiting for an Agricultural Instructor to review. Treat them as helpful guidance, not official rules.
ak.method.kw: method|how does it work|methodology|architecture|pipeline|rule engine|how it is built|approach|design|modules
ak.method.a: Three separate parts that share only JSON files: a data pipeline (Python) fetches NASA and other data, a rule engine turns it into the signal and crop advice, and the website shows it in plain words with sources. Every threshold sits in a config file, and each crop number has a source and a confidence level.
ak.tests_summary.kw: tests|validation|accuracy|how accurate is it|backtest|does it work|evidence|test results|how good is it|performance
ak.tests_summary.a: Rain-fed crop advice was right {acc}% of the time against {guess}% for simply guessing (averaged over {n} crop tests; learned from 1981 to 2010, tested on 2011 to 2025). The El Niño outlook made {hits} correct calls out of {calls} and does not beat its baseline. The tank-water model: {verdict} All of this is saved honestly in data/validation.json, good and bad results alike.
ak.el_nino_result.kw: el nino result|el nino test|does el nino help|el nino accuracy|el nino predict|enso test|el nino outlook|el nino work|did el nino work
ak.el_nino_result.q: Did the El Niño outlook work?
ak.el_nino_result.a: No. It made {hits} correct calls out of {calls} and does not beat its baseline, so the site shows it only as a count and does not use it for advice. Several tanks share one rain square, so those results are the same test counted more than once.
ak.tank_model_result.kw: tank model|water model|tank water model|water prediction|water forecast model|model result
ak.tank_model_result.a: {verdict} (mean error {model} points for the model against {base} for the baseline, over {tested} tanks tested.) So it is not used for advice.
ak.crop_accuracy.kw: crop accuracy|crop advice accuracy|how good is the crop advice|crop advice test|mung bean accuracy|good was right|beats guessing
ak.crop_accuracy.q: How good is the crop advice?
ak.crop_accuracy.a: On rain-fed crops it was right {acc}% of the time against {guess}% for guessing ({n} crop tests, tested on 2011 to 2025 after learning from 1981 to 2010). The full table per crop is on the Research page.
ak.known_issues.kw: known issues|problems|limitations|weaknesses|what is wrong|data problems|bugs|caveats|24 times|geosit|too large
ak.known_issues.a: NASA POWER's near-real-time rain from 1 October 2026 is about 24 times too large, so we skip it and rain data ends on 30 September 2026. POWER rain before 1997 looks too low at some places. Many tanks share one 50 km rain square, so they show identical rain. Real satellite tank water exists for only a few tanks so far. The Sinhala text still needs a native-speaker review.
ak.reproduce.kw: reproduce|reproduce the results|run it myself|source code|code|github|repository|how to run|rerun|open source|licence|license
ak.reproduce.a: Yes. The code and every saved data file are in the project. Run the pipeline steps in order (rain, forecast, water, rules, crops, seasonal, ndvi, advisory, finish) and then the validation step; the tests run with pytest. Each source's licence is on the Data sources page.
ak.credits.kw: credits|image credits|picture credits|who made the pictures|attribution|acknowledgements|photos|licence of images
ak.credits.q: Where do the pictures come from?
ak.credits.a: The Image credits page lists where every picture comes from, including the ones made with AI, and their licences.
ak.how_verdict.kw: how is dry maybe wet decided|verdict|how do you decide|dry maybe wet|what does dry mean|what does wet mean|rain rule|how does it decide|will it rain
ak.how_verdict.q: How do you decide Dry, Maybe or Wet?
ak.how_verdict.a: For your chosen hours it adds up the forecast rain. Wet means about 3 mm or more, or a 70% chance or more. Maybe means about 0.5 mm or more, or a 35% chance or more. Otherwise it says Dry. These are simple draft rules of thumb, not an official standard.
ak.best_time.kw: best time|best day|best hours|driest hours|when should i go|which day is best|best window|top days|recommend a day
ak.best_time.q: What is the best time or day?
ak.best_time.a: For the day you pick, the page shows the driest 3 hours. It also ranks the next 16 days for your hours and lists the 3 best days, with Dry first and then the least rain.
ak.trip_kinds.kw: kind of trip|trip type|hike|wedding|beach|sports match|outdoor event|farm visit|cricket|picnic|event type
ak.trip_kinds.q: What kinds of trip can I plan?
ak.trip_kinds.a: Choose any trip, hike or walk, beach or river, outdoor event or wedding, sports match, or farm visit. Each sets its usual hours, which you can still change, and adds hints such as strong shoes for a hike or boots for field work.
ak.wind_uv_heat.kw: wind|uv|uv index|heat|feels like|too hot|gusts|sunburn|sunscreen|how windy|sun strength|hot weather
ak.wind_uv_heat.q: How do you judge wind, sun and heat?
ak.wind_uv_heat.a: For your hours: wind gusts of 40 km/h or more are flagged windy and 60 km/h or more strong; the sun uses the World Health Organization UV bands (6 high, 8 very high, 11 extreme); 'feels like' temperatures of 38°C or more are hot and 41°C or more very hot. The wind and heat levels are draft round numbers for planning, not an official standard.
ak.usual_month.kw: usual rain|what is this month usually like|average rain|usual weather|climate|normal rain|month average|typical weather|usual temperature
ak.usual_month.q: What is this month usually like?
ak.usual_month.a: It is the NASA POWER average for 2001 to 2025 for the 50 km square around the place: the usual rain for the month and the usual hottest days. A few places do not have a saved value yet, and then the page says so.
ak.compare_places.kw: compare|compare places|two places|which place is better|compare two|better place|versus|which is drier
ak.compare_places.a: Yes. Under 'Compare two places' pick a second place and the page shows both for the same day and hours: the verdict, rain, chance of rain and wind gusts, and says which looks better.
ak.calendar_file.kw: calendar|add to calendar|ics|google calendar|reminder|save the date|calendar file
ak.calendar_file.q: Can I add it to my calendar?
ak.calendar_file.a: Yes. 'Add to my calendar' downloads a calendar file (.ics) for your day and hours, with the verdict in the notes. Open it with your phone or computer calendar.
ak.forecast_uncertainty.kw: how reliable|how accurate is the forecast|will the forecast change|forecast far ahead|is the forecast certain|16 days|trust the forecast|uncertain
ak.forecast_uncertainty.a: It is a weather-model forecast from Open-Meteo (not NASA, not radar). It is best for the next few days and less certain after the first week, so for a big event check again close to the day.
ak.plan_sources.kw: where does the weather come from|which service|data source|where is the weather from|source of forecast|who gives the forecast|nasa
ak.plan_sources.q: Where does the weather come from?
ak.plan_sources.a: The forecast is from Open-Meteo (not NASA data). The usual rain and heat for the month are from NASA POWER, and the map is NASA GIBS satellite imagery.
ak.share_plan.kw: share|share this plan|send plan|whatsapp|copy link|link|send to friends
ak.share_plan.q: How do I share the plan?
ak.share_plan.a: The page address holds your place, day, hours and kind of trip, so copying the link shares the whole plan. There are also WhatsApp and Copy buttons.
ak.did_you_mean: I am not sure what you mean. Did you mean one of these?
ak.src.written: Written answer, checked against the site's data
ak.src.data: The saved tank files on this site
